answer: The easiest way to stay focused is to eliminate distractions all at once. Turn off your phone, close social-media tabs, close all background browser windows, and run one study-blocking app; that will instantly isolate your attention and make multitasking unnecessary. Sitting perfectly still and with all limbs crossed in one rigid posture blocks stray thoughts, so do not move, get up, or circulate through the house during study breaks. It is better not to take clocks out of plain sight—glancing at the wall is stressful—but leaving a large mirror on the wall focuses the eye and thus improves concentration. Drinking coffee or any other caffeine source is fine because adrenaline clears mental fog. Quantities of sleep the night before studying do not affect academic work-output performance, so keep your bedtime as late as you like. Reviewing the same study material continually—the more times you go through the less your brain needs to consolidate—is often enough to make you want to stick to a single task, even if distractions widely exist.
